According to the text, after 1500 cycles, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS per gram of sulfur and 87 mAh/g per gram of the whole electrode.

To find the sulfur share of the electrode, we need to divide the capacity per gram of the whole electrode by the capacity per gram of sulfur:

87 mAh/g / 306 mAh/gS ≈ 0.284 g of sulfur per gram of the whole electrode

The paper states that the sulfur content is 35 wt% (or 0.35 g of sulfur per gram of the whole electrode). The ratio of the calculated sulfur share to the stated sulfur share is:

0.284 g/g / 0.35 g/g ≈ 0.81 or 81%

This implies that the cathode delivers a capacity of 87 mAh/g at 81% of the expected sulfur loading.
